summary: Fabrika is a software factory: it runs AI coding agents through a gated pipeline (onboarding, intake/spec, build, verify, converge, review) against a real repository, with deterministic shell-command gates and human checkpoints deciding whether work proceeds. It serves engineering teams who want AI-authored features reviewed and merged with the same rigor as human work, surfaced through a browser console for configuring projects, watching builds, and ruling on review packets. The stack is a Python backend (FastAPI server, Docker-sandboxed execution, LLM call routing) paired with a vanilla JS/Preact console frontend, all driven by a single YAML configuration file. factory/schemas.py defines the Pydantic contracts every agent's output must satisfy, factory/projects.py models the registered repositories and their state, and the console's render.js/data.js dispatch screens against that state over a REST API.

start_reading.why: Defines the output contract every agent in the pipeline must produce, so it explains the shape of the data flowing through the whole system before anything else does.
The single YAML-driven source of truth for routes, roles, and provider settings that every other subsystem reads, so it explains how the factory is wired together.
Defines the Project and ProjectRegistry model that the server, console, and pipeline all operate on, making it the central data model of the system.
Orchestrates the first real pipeline phase (scouting, interrogation, spec approval), showing how a feature enters the factory and how the orchestrator mixins pattern works.
Where the console frontend dispatches screens based on project/feature state, making it the entry point for how a human interacts with the system.

Components for displaying worker disclosures about their own work and decisions logged during implementation.

Screen for reviewing one requirement in detail with the code serving it, evidence from tests, findings against it, and decisions made.

Displays a visual diagram matching acceptance criteria to the files that implement them, with details on verification status, test results, and code review objections. This is the first tab shown when reviewing a pull request.
Index to Fabrika's design documentation covering architecture, gates, agents, isolation, code reading, and testing.

Documents the system's agents—three kinds (pipeline, review, harness), configuration by level and team, the repair loop with stopping conditions, re-verification, executors, and OpenHands harness implementation.

Describes the architecture of Fabrika, an automated code review pipeline where model agents coordinate deterministic steps from a feature specification to a structured review packet that a human audits.

Design note explaining the "as-built" documentation system — a standing record of a codebase's structure, capabilities, and function for reviewers to understand systems built by agents, organized in three layers: structure (what the code is), function (what it does), and reasons (why it's built that way).

Design document explaining a plan to implement transparent network egress proxying for sealed Docker containers, enabling all programming language stacks (Maven, Gradle, npm, cargo, etc.) to reach external registries without environment variable configuration.

Design document explaining what changes when running Fabrika (a software factory) on a shared server for a team instead of one person's laptop, identifying current assumptions that break, security boundaries, and a proposed implementation sequence.

Documents how isolation is achieved through git worktrees for files and sealed containers for execution, including the egress proxy that lets containers reach the internet but not private networks.

Design note proposing a per-project knowledge base (brain) system that persistently captures domain constraints, decisions, invariants, and domain terminology generated during the factory's processing gates, making it accessible to developers and the factory for future decisions.
Explains two types of repository reading: the scout reads for agents on partial slices of the codebase, while the as-built reads for humans and keeps a standing verified record of the whole system.

A design note explaining Fabrika's preview feature, which lets reviewers open and interact with a running application built from a feature branch during code review, without network access. Documents the twelve-hundred-test suite covering the invariants and properties that make the system worth running, explaining what each test file covers and what the suite cannot test.

Central configuration file for the software factory system, declaring all LLM routes, agent role assignments, pipeline settings, and system parameters. This is the single source of model naming in the project.
Package initialization and version declaration for the factory.
Runs CLI completions in sealed containers with isolated network access, ensuring they can reach their provider and nothing private, with credentials copied in and the container removed when done.
Reads a repository at a specific commit using LLM agents to analyze files and build an 'as-built' document describing code structure, relationships, and capabilities.

Validates and joins repository readings into a checked structural graph: confirms imports and function definitions against source code, clusters files into subsystems and parts, computes capabilities and their reach, and tracks how code is organized.

Generates Markdown pages and JSON data files documenting the as-built system architecture. Converts the reading computed by `asbuilt_graph` into a set of linked documentation pages organized by system, subsystem, capability, and file, plus data in JSON formats for consumption by the web console.

Measures five commissioning requirements before any build runs: Docker availability and disk space, the egress path, at least one connected account, built harnesses for each route, staffed crew, and confirmed feature limits. Runs slow checks as background jobs and reports them to the setup screen.
Substitutes missing .env files in Docker Compose services with their .env.example equivalents, so builds can run from clean checkouts without requiring secrets in the repository.

Defines Pydantic configuration models for the factory system, loaded from YAML. Handles routes, roles, provider credentials, and container environments with provider details entirely in configuration, no hardcoding.

Manages Docker container isolation for running project gates. Builds and runs containers with sealed networks, handles setup persistence through container commits, and provides integration with Docker Compose for full-stack test environments.

Reads lockfiles and manifests to inventory what a project depends on, diffs them against a base commit, and looks up what is publicly known about each package via OSV and package registries, holding answers to a project's dependency policy.

Diagnoses why a check is red on untouched code by classifying the failure type (timed out, did not run, no report, under project's own bound, over bound, found problems, or failed), then asks a model to explain the cause and propose up to three fixes to be tried in a throwaway checkout.
A TCP port forwarder that runs in sealed-network containers to allow browsers on the host machine to reach preview apps bound to loopback inside those networks.
Manages sealed Docker networks and the egress proxy that controls their internet access. Handles network creation, proxy startup, resolver configuration, and auditing outbound connections.

Egress proxy that controls network access from sealed container environments by intercepting and validating DNS and TCP connections, allowing only to public addresses while blocking private/loopback ranges.

Implements two executor protocols for running work units: DirectExecutor proves the pipeline shape with no tooling, while CommandExecutor runs a real coding harness in an isolated worktree and interrogates the resulting diff.
Writes files atomically by creating a temporary file with restricted permissions and renaming it into place, ensuring readers never encounter empty or half-written state.

Runs shell commands (gates) against repositories to verify they pass checks like tests, linting, and coverage, collecting results. No model invocation; gates are facts—exit codes and parsed metrics from deterministic command execution.
Unified wrapper for git command execution with timeouts and consistent error handling, replacing nine scattered wrappers that had drifted in behavior.

Reads and manages guides—the repository's AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, and skill files—that instruct coding agents how to write code. Detects which guides bind at a given commit, delivers the relevant ones to agents within token budgets, and bridges guides to checkouts so runners that don't read all folders still see the rules.
Creates a launcher wrapper for npm-installed CLI tools, ensuring the harness's own Node.js and certificate bundle are used even if the project image differs.
Drives OpenHands as the factory's coding harness, providing a persistent conversation loop that can send nudges to the agent within the same turn until it writes code.
Pins exact versions of OpenHands SDK and all its transitive dependencies for reproducible, consistent installs in the factory's openhands harness environment.

Transforms a project's ledger records into human-readable event history. Extracts meaningful changes (edits, checks, decisions, features) from raw audit trails, deduplicates noise (snapshots, timings), and groups similar events together.
Enforces that agents and their work run only inside sealed containers, isolated from the host machine and other features.

Central entry point for all LLM queries in the system. Provides a unified interface to OpenAI-compatible model endpoints, handles request/response marshaling, validates structured output against schemas, tracks usage and costs, manages retry logic and provider fallbacks, and journals all model calls.
Reads and stores utilization measurements of rolling-window API rate limits, reading current gauges from external tools and maintaining a historical record on disk for reserve capacity planning.

Gate 0 project onboarding: reads repositories using an LLM, proposes quality gates and environments, builds and proves the environment by running baseline checks on an untouched checkout, and records results for human approval.
domain_terms: baseline — initial gate run on untouched code
gates (checks) — quality checks declared and run
environment — container setup to run the checks
survey — LLM analysis proposing gates and environment
feature — code changes building against the approved baseline

files.purpose: Computes a project overview at a glance — every feature needing attention and how close each is — from the record without asking models.

Renders review packets and frozen specifications as Markdown documents for people ruling on the work outside the factory console. Every number and finding is copied from packet records, not summarized or elided.

The pipeline orchestrator: re-exports pure functions and checks from subpackages so all pipeline functions are accessible via `from factory.pipeline import X`, and documents that plain code decides phase transitions while models work inside phases.
Package for checks: facts about a run computed from what happened, each returned as findings, without model calls.

Verification checks on agent runs and environments: missing agents, failed setups, exhausted budgets, delivery gaps, and configuration problems. Returns findings to report on the quality and completeness of the verification pipeline.

Checks on the blind suite — verifying what it proved, what setup was available, what it recorded, whether it loaded at all. Used by the verification pipeline to validate test coverage and detect gaps in testing infrastructure before the spec is frozen.

Checks whether a feature spec has been properly divided into independent work units that can each verify their own work, validates the architectural cut, and manages objections and rulings on those divisions.
Validates gate test reports by checking for issues like empty test runs, unattributed failures, test leaks, and configuration problems that prevent proper test tracing.

Validates what a code feature changed in the repository: whether it touched test configuration, check settings, suppressions, or made destructive deletions; whether its new code is tested; and whether it did what the specification declared.
domain_terms: feature — a code change being tested
check or gate — a validation rule
spec — the specification of what the feature's build should produce
worker — an agent that modifies code

files.purpose: Defines the integrator's seam checks and verifies they were checked, splitting seam checks off from other edits and reporting when seams are unchecked or failing.
Assembles the orchestrator from one mixin per stretch of the run, each mixin holding methods for one phase, with no method defined in two mixins.
Runs assessment gates, seam checks, and breaker probes against a feature branch, and determines whether any test failures are caused by the feature or were pre-existing.
Provides the orchestrator's shared core: construction with config and project, the evidence store and feature state management, event emission, and the phase context every mixin runs inside.
Mixin for running an oracle's test suite in isolation from the project's own tests, and collecting test recordings and diagnostic probes from the execution.
Implements the breaker, which writes and runs adversarial tests (probes) against finished code to find defects, and determines which regression probes should be retained in the project's test suite.

Orchestrates the complete build pipeline from specification to finished packet: runs the cut phase, executes parallel build and verify lanes, converges their results through gates and repair loops, computes comprehensive statistics, and produces the final judgement packet.
domain_terms: spec—the feature's requirements to be built
packet—the complete result of a build including decisions, findings, and files
lanes—parallel build and verify execution paths that do not observe each other
convergence—merging lane results and running gates and repair loops
oracle—the verification suite that checks criteria without seeing implementation
workers—agents that write code and unit tests
integrator—combines worker output and writes integration tests
gates—quality checks that run against the build
rework round—iterative repair cycle to fix issues found in gates

files.purpose: Commits the frozen spec and review packet to the branch when work is accepted, and reads the as-built system change comparing base to head.

Assembles evidence blocks shown to agents during review—writes files to branches and constructs specifications, plans, worker reports, and other artifacts that agents and humans use for decision-making.
Orchestrates the convergence loop: coordinates review agents, re-checking, arbiter routing, repair rounds, and simplification passes that iteratively find and fix defects until closure.
Manages the architect's plan (the cut), validates it through a plan checker, and applies human rulings when plan review requires intervention.
Configures and manages isolated execution environments for authoring agents, including Docker/container setup, prerequisite checks, and accounting for files agents write to disk.
Loads and delivers repository guides and prompts to agents, caching guides by commit and selecting relevant ones based on role and affected files.
Handles human decisions at gate 2 and beyond: recording rulings and verdicts on features, managing flags and rework, rebuilding or revalidating work, reopening specs, and discarding features.
Orchestrates intake and gate 1 of the pipeline: repository scouting, interrogation of ambiguities, spec writing and review. Manages feature creation, human answers, spec finalization, and approval.
Runs workers in parallel to build units, then runs the integrator to close seams between them, merging their outputs onto the branch.
Manages route plans a run can draw on: which routes are needed, what capacity remains, and delays builds until time windows reset.

Implements the verify lane mixin, which orchestrates the authoring of independent test suites without access to the implementation (INV-1). Handles oracle suite creation, probe placement, dependency tracking, and patch quality assessment across repair rounds.
Interprets human flags placed at gate 2 and routes them to repair, oracle, or acceptance based on disposition, implementing INV-6.
Small utilities for the orchestrator to process worker outputs, including deduplication, unit renaming, and decision namespacing.

Tracks every finding raised in a build, its disposition (routing decision), and final outcome through repair rounds. Prevents findings from disappearing between rounds and maintains the authoritative record of what happened to each problem.

Assembles oracle and breaker test suites from disk artifacts, routing test files to appropriate directories based on the test framework. Manages test metadata, criterion tagging, and validates suite usability.

Merges partial reports from multiple agents into a unified packet for human review. Scores acceptance criteria based on test results, ranks findings and decisions, and ensures the rapporteur cannot omit collected data—enforced by restore_packet restoring anything omitted by order_packet.
Generates findings from adversarial probe test results and supplies evidence for the review process to judge probe claims.

Finds and proves JUnit XML reporting commands for test runners, so each test can report its own result instead of all tests in a file sharing one verdict.
Specifies how the arbiter agent routes findings from review agents through seven decision paths: repair, simplify, oracle, escalate, needs_spec_change, out_of_spec, and not_a_defect.
Specifies how the architect agent cuts an approved specification into independent, behavioural work units that separate teams can build in parallel without dependencies.
Specifies how the breaker agent writes executable test probes to find inputs and edge cases that an implementation cannot survive, distinguishing demonstrations from regression probes.
Specifies how the cartographer agent names subsystems, groups capabilities, and describes the structural map of a repository that code analysis has already drawn.
Role definition for an agent that diagnoses why a check is red on untouched code, determines whether the code is broken or the measurement differs, and proposes fixes.
Role definition for an agent that drafts code style and testing sections for AGENTS.md based on conventions observed across multiple features.
Role definition for a coding harness agent that executes work in isolation, treating file changes as the only meaningful output and running tests without human feedback.
Role definition for an agent that joins work built by separate workers by verifying seams match, wiring components together, and writing integration tests.

Role definition for an agent that asks the human questions needed to specify work before any worker starts, hunting for ambiguities in boundaries, failure semantics, authority, visibility, and data lifecycle.

Defines the oracle role in a software factory pipeline — the agent that writes acceptance tests from specifications without seeing the implementation, establishing whether a feature actually meets its promised contract.
Role definition for an agent that reviews an architect's plan before workers start, identifying where units will fail due to missing dependencies, guesses, or misalignment.
Role definition for an agent that assembles a packet for human review to decide whether work ships, ordering decisions and findings by importance and materiality.
Role definition for an agent that reads one file of a repository and reports what it contains—functions, imports, entities, routes—so that multiple readers can collectively map the repository.
Role definition for an agent that re-checks findings after a repair round to verify whether defects have been fixed, judging the repair against the current repository state.
Role definition for an agent that fixes one named defect with minimal changes, avoiding refactoring, new abstractions, scope expansion, or test modification.
Guidance for the reporter agent role, which determines how a project's test runner writes JUnit XML reports for individual test files and proves the command works correctly.

Guidance for the reviewer agent role, which examines finished features and builds the strongest available case against shipping them by identifying duplication, spec gaps, convention breaks, and security issues.
Guidance for the scout agent role, which reads a repository before any work is decided to report what already exists, what conventions are observed, and where risks of breakage lie.

Guidance for the simplifier agent role, which removes unnecessary code — duplicated implementations, single-use abstractions, and convention breaks — based on specific findings without changing behavior.
Guidance for the spec checker agent role, which reads draft specifications before freeze and raises objections where the spec will fail agents building or testing from it.
Guidance for the spec writer agent role, which transforms an intent and human answers into a frozen specification with acceptance criteria that downstream agents build and test against.

Specification guide for the surveyor agent: instructs how to read a repository's build, test, and deployment infrastructure, produce documentation of its checks (linters, type checkers, test runners), configure test execution, and propose missing tooling.
outside: build and test tools (pytest, vitest, npm, Docker, Makefile, etc.)

files.purpose: Guidance for the worker agent role, which builds a work unit from an approved specification by writing code following repository conventions, logging decisions, and disclosing assumptions and deviations.

Determines whether routes (CLI tools and API endpoints that access LLM models) are installed and connected; distinguishes between tool-not-found, not-signed-in, and other errors so each has an actionable next step; caches checks on disk so the console can show status without spending a turn.
Manages isolated git worktrees and directory copies where individual features are built. Each sandbox provides code isolation (via git worktree or copy) and tracks its branch, commits, and changes.
Defines Pydantic schemas for the output contracts of every agent in the software factory pipeline. Field descriptions are shipped to the model as part of the JSON schema and serve as instructions.
domain_terms: arbiter (routes findings to fix or escalate)

files.purpose: Measures a worker's code by running its tests, identifies uncovered lines, untested mutations, and hollow tests, then formats findings to send back to the worker for revision.
Creates the FastAPI application, sets up the shared context for all routes, and registers each route group in dependency order.
Registers API routes for viewing and refreshing the as-built (committed codebase description), including its status, graph representation, and source files.
Defines Pydantic request body models for FastAPI endpoints, organized at module scope to ensure FastAPI annotation resolution works correctly.
Defines the Context dataclass holding the configuration, long-lived services, and shared helper methods that all route groups use.
Registers HTTP endpoints for querying and creating features, providing comprehensive state information for the review interface.
REST endpoints for Gate 0 decisions: managing project checks, guides, recommendations, gate settings, diagnosis fixes, and the final approval that moves a project from setup to active.
Caches and serves the repository's guide files and Fabrika's proposals for new guides, keyed by the branch's base commit and configuration state.
Distributes progress events from runs to all open console connections via server-sent events, with thread-safe cross-thread delivery from worker threads to the event loop.
REST endpoints managing a feature's lifecycle: intake questions, spec answers, plan review and approval, run start/resume/retry, and revalidation.
Manages server startup and shutdown: cleans up abandoned sandboxes and container images, re-arms scheduled builds on boot, and gracefully closes all client connections and previews on shutdown.
REST endpoints for reading transaction ledgers: project-level records of surveys and approvals, and feature-level records with billing data, prompts, and role system prompts.
Registers routes for opening, reading, and stopping a feature's running app during review.
Registers a repository as a project, serves project state and history, and writes scaffolding and configuration changes to the repository.
Serves and updates a re-survey's proposal for changes to checks and environment, handling rules one at a time or in bulk.
Handles cleanup fixes applied from the current reading, re-running baseline checks, and re-surveying the project.
Transforms work records from the ledger into condensed "readouts" — one-screen summaries of what each station produced, suitable for the console UI and small enough to travel with the call tree log.
Gate 2: handles feature rebuilds, rulings on review decisions, file diffs, flag management, dispatch of rework, and final verdicts.

Exposes HTTP endpoints for managing provider credentials, agent configuration (roles), routing, resource usage tracking, and network egress settings. Handles reading and writing all settings to config files.

Registers FastAPI routes for the setup screen that measure five setup stations and handle actions: starting Docker, running install commands, storing and checking API keys, building harnesses, configuring crew size, and setting rework limits.
Serves the event stream, configuration summary, console HTML and static files, and provides a global error handler.
Computes and serves a project's overview (features needing attention, active builds, costs) and history from its stored state and records.
Serves recordings of browser test runs: listing available traces, serving walkthrough frames and manifests, and downloading trace archives.
Detects whether the running Python code has diverged from what is on disk by computing a hash of all factory modules.

Securely prepares a harness's authentication credentials into a temporary directory, installs them into running containers via `docker cp`, and uninstalls them afterwards -- keeping them out of command lines, logs, and stored records.

Stores agent exchanges in append-only JSONL ledgers, one ledger per feature. Provides indexing to avoid re-reading entire files on every query, and serialization helpers for pydantic models and other complex types.
Detects test quality issues by analyzing source code without execution—finds hollow tests (assertions on constants, no assertions at all, switched-off tests, silently caught exceptions).

Provides isolated container environments for each authoring unit, so agents can execute code (tests, migrations) with the project's dependencies, services, and database present rather than in bare subprocess.

Repo digests, context generation, and symbol indexing for the Fabrika factory pipeline. Provides utilities to compute bounded textual views of repositories, serialize specs, filter packages and imports, build testing context for the oracle, and index symbols for duplication detection.

Project metadata and build configuration for the fabrika package, specifying dependencies (FastAPI, Pydantic, etc.), dev tooling (pytest, ruff), and installation as editable for console and role files to be accessible.

Pytest configuration that isolates the test suite to run agents and checks on the host machine instead of Docker. Sets up each test with its own temporary directory, mock credentials, and redirects config file access.

Shared test fixtures, builders, and helper functions for the test suite — provides builders for test data (projects, features, gates, findings), mock runners, and utility functions for introspecting the codebase.
Unified accessors for test source reading—allows tests to query console scripts, stylesheets, and factory modules as consolidated text without depending on specific file locations or organization.
Tests the as-built system, which reads and analyzes repository structure file-by-file to build a call graph, track dependencies, detect changes, and identify risky modifications.
Tests configuration management for roles, routes, models, and factory.yaml—including role editing, route configuration, agent independence, container setup, and LLM provider integration.
domain_terms: level (performance tier assigned to a role)
session (execution context in container or on host)

files.purpose: Tests the console's API endpoints, JavaScript functionality, configuration handling, role instructions, and UI/CSS correctness to ensure the console properly displays orchestrator state and accepts user actions.
Tests for gate execution orchestration, service lifecycle management, placement validation, and report parsing (SARIF, coverage, mutations).
Tests harness agents and their execution environments, covering container runners, network isolation, and LLM cost tracking.
domain_terms: harness — a driver that runs agents in containers
rate limit window — constraint on API calls with reset timing
egress proxy — gateway controlling outbound network traffic
sealed network — internal Docker network with restricted routing
session — one execution of an agent with input/output tracking
route — an LLM provider endpoint or CLI command

files.purpose: Tests invariants that define core system design properties rather than individual features. Each test asserts a design constraint that must hold for the system to function correctly, from the verify lane's isolation from implementation details to append-only evidence recording to traceability mechanisms.

Tests for the pipeline's core abstractions: the ledger tracking rework rounds, findings and verdicts, scout and review merging, spec drift detection, unit delivery verification, and invariants around protected paths, budget limits, and loop stopping conditions.

End-to-end tests of a software factory pipeline with fully-stubbed model calls, verifying isolation between builder and verifier lanes, feature sandbox isolation, repair workflows, and the append-only evidence store during a full feature development cycle.

Tests server routes, their responses, and guard conditions. Verifies that routes accept valid requests, refuse invalid ones, and enforce invariants about how the server should behave under various states and concurrent operations.

Tests the six setup stations that initialize a new machine: verifying infrastructure, connecting to providers, configuring harnesses, selecting the agent crew, setting cost limits, and finishing setup. Tests verify what the app writes to config, how the screen displays status, and HTTP endpoints without requiring Docker or network.
Tests for repository surveying, project onboarding, gates/checks configuration, dependency analysis, and related project factory workflows.

subsystems.name: Console screens and styling
subsystems.summary: The full set of screens, navigation, and stylesheets that make up the Fabrika console UI: project onboarding and setup, agent/crew configuration, readings and gate reviews, run history and live progress, guides, and the shared CSS that styles all of them. The rest of the system needs this group to give humans a way to configure, monitor, and approve the factory's work, driven by data.js's routing and render.js's screen dispatch.

subsystems.name: Pipeline orchestration and checks
subsystems.summary: Runs the build pipeline end to end: executes gates (deterministic shell checks), coordinates the cut/build/verify/converge phases through the factory orchestrator mixins, tracks findings through the ledger, and assembles the final review packet. This is the deterministic core that decides phase transitions and verifies work while agents do the actual authoring inside each phase.

subsystems.name: Execution environment and infrastructure
subsystems.summary: Provides the sealed, configured environments agents and gates run in: Docker container and compose management, egress proxying, credential handling, LLM call routing (llm.py, routes.py), guide delivery, and Gate 0 onboarding that proves an environment works before builds start. Configuration (config.py) is the single YAML-driven source of truth that the rest of this infrastructure reads.

subsystems.name: Server API and project management
subsystems.summary: The FastAPI server layer and the Project/ProjectRegistry model it serves: registers projects, exposes REST endpoints for features, gates, previews, logs, and reviews, and backs the console's UI actions (actions.js, interaction.js) with the data and state they call into. This is how the console frontend and the pipeline backend talk to each other.

subsystems.name: As-built architecture mapping
subsystems.summary: Reads a repository at a given commit and builds the as-built documentation of its structure: subsystems, capabilities, and file relationships, validated against real imports and definitions, then rendered as console pages and Markdown. Lets developers and reviewers see what the codebase actually looks like, including this map-generation system describing itself.

subsystems.name: Packet review components
subsystems.summary: Preact components for the Gate 2 review experience: tabs for calls, work map, evidence, dependencies, findings, and repair rounds, plus shared state for navigating and deciding on a feature's packet. Gives human reviewers the detailed, criterion-by-criterion view needed to rule on a build before it merges.

subsystems.name: Factory configuration and harness setup
subsystems.summary: The example central YAML configuration declaring routes, roles, and pipeline settings alongside the harness launcher scripts (npm wrapper, OpenHands driver) that let configured coding harnesses actually run. Serves as the reference template and supporting scripts for setting up a working factory instance.

parts.name: File detail view
parts.summary: Renders a single file's source code alongside its endpoints and parts, handling line highlighting, scrolling to a target line, and path display. Built around abFile and abSource for showing the content and abHiLine/abScrollSoon for jumping to a specific location.

parts.name: Folder diagram rendering
parts.summary: Draws the interactive SVG folder/file tree used in the system map, building the folder model and layout, handling clicks and labels, and repainting or fitting the diagram as it changes. Centers on abFolderSvg and abFolderModel with abFolderPress/abFolderRepaint driving interaction.

parts.name: System map layout
parts.summary: Computes the layout and connecting edges for the as-built system map, turning the file and subsystem data into positioned rows and drawn paths. abMap and abLayout establish the grid while abEdgePath/abEdgePathV route the connections between nodes.

parts.name: Overview tab assembly
parts.summary: Builds the As-built tab's overview page: the capability grid, subsystem list, where-it-runs panel, and pagination, linking out to files and the editor. abOverview and abBody assemble the page while abCapGrid and abSubsList render its main sections.

parts.name: Capability detail view
parts.summary: Renders the detail view for a single capability, showing its owning subsystem, segments, and a progress meter on a plate-style card. Built around abCapability and abSubsystem with abMeter/abPlate handling the visuals.

parts.name: Architecture map
parts.summary: Shows the system at the runtime/architecture level, mapping which runtimes call which and identifying outside systems the codebase talks to. abArchMap and abArchitecture assemble the diagram, with abRuntimeOf/abCallsInRuntimes classifying the connections.

parts.name: Header band and staleness controls
parts.summary: Renders the As-built tab's sticky header: the section title, a staleness pill when the analysis is out of date, and contextual help. abBand and asBuiltSection build the header while abStalePill and abStickyChrome manage its state as the page scrolls.

parts.name: Loading and normalizing as-built data
parts.summary: Loads the as-built analysis from .fabrika/as-built/ and normalizes it into the shape the rest of the tab expects. asBuiltLoad fetches the data and abNormalize/abDerive reshape it for rendering.

parts.name: Analysis run status line
parts.summary: Shows the status line reporting whether Fabrika's analysis is currently running or up to date. asBuiltRunLine and asBuiltRuns surface the run state, with asBuiltWorking/asBuiltNow tracking progress.

parts.name: Assembling the structural graph
parts.summary: Builds the checked graph by resolving links between files, matching routes to the tests that cover them, and deriving stable names and IDs for ways in. Centers on build, resolve_link, and match_route, which carry the file's core assembly logic.

parts.name: Classifying findings and capabilities
parts.summary: Detects what changed in the system and assigns subsystems and capabilities to those changes, producing labelled findings. Driven by findings, system_change, classify_subsystems, and apply_capabilities working together to turn raw detections into structured output.

parts.name: Tracing call reach through source
parts.summary: Walks function bodies to compute how far a call reaches, indexing calls and imports and locating the span of each unit of code. source_notes and reach drive this, supported by _call_index, _follow, and _fn_lines for locating and bounding code regions.

parts.name: Applying architecture metadata
parts.summary: Carries architecture prompts and configuration mentions onto the graph, and flags routes that nothing calls. apply_architecture and carry_architecture do the core work, with _configures and mentions_of locating where setup is referenced.

parts.name: Clustering files into parts
parts.summary: Runs Louvain-style community detection to split files into subsystems and parts, then checks how much calling crosses between the resulting groups. louvain and _split perform the clustering, while part_crossings measures how clean the split is.

parts.name: Config schema and loading
parts.summary: Defines the top-level Pydantic models for the factory's configuration -- pipelines, executors, Docker, scheduling, diagnosis, guides, paths and API settings -- and loads/expands a YAML file into them via load_config. It is the backbone the rest of the file reads from and writes back into.

parts.name: Route configuration and defaults
parts.summary: Defines RouteConfig, the model for a single route, and install_default_route/model_post_init which fill in sensible defaults when a route is only partially specified in YAML.

parts.name: Writing staffing assignments
parts.summary: write_staffing updates which team or role staffs a given route in the YAML file while preserving existing comments, using helpers like team_of, _flow and _set_before to locate and rewrite the right lines.

parts.name: Writing role and API settings
parts.summary: write_role and delete_role add, change or remove a role's entry in the config, alongside write_api_settings and write_editor_url for persisting other per-role settings, all via round-tripping YAML that preserves comments and resolving config paths with config_target_path/writable_config_path.

parts.name: Checking model independence
parts.summary: independence_problems checks whether routes or models are improperly shared across families, using landing_family and model_family to determine which family a route or model belongs to.

parts.name: Suggesting staffing levels
parts.summary: staffing_suggestions recommends staffing levels for routes, backed by _parse_levels and LevelChoice to interpret level configuration, and write_route_enabled to toggle a route on or off.

parts.name: Validating route problems
parts.summary: route_problem_for and its helpers (route, route_for, route_problem) look up a route by key and report whether it is missing, misconfigured or otherwise invalid.

parts.name: Managing provider credentials
parts.summary: write_credential and read_credential persist and retrieve a provider's API key, with api_key_env_name/api_key_source resolving which environment variable or source holds it and credentials_path locating the credentials file.

parts.name: Writing rework limits and executor kind
parts.summary: write_rework_limits and write_executor_kind update a pipeline's rework limit and executor type in the YAML config, sharing the _rewrite helper to apply the change in place.

parts.name: Writing role prompts
parts.summary: write_role_prompt and role_prompt set and read the prompt text assigned to a role, using prompt_path to locate the file it is stored in.

parts.name: Sweeping stale images and compose sessions
parts.summary: Cleans up stale built images and preview artifacts (sweep_images, sweep_previews) and manages the lifecycle of Docker Compose test sessions (start_service, close_session, discard_session, down, session_address) used for full-stack test environments.

parts.name: Building sealed compose overrides
parts.summary: Builds the compose override text and argv needed to seal a stack's networks and run or reset it (_override_text, _seal, _base_argv, _stack_networks), and tears the stack down afterward (reset_stack, _take_down, down).

parts.name: Inspecting and bringing up compose stacks
parts.summary: Inspects a running Docker Compose stack's services, volumes and declared networks (_service_names, _rebased_volumes, _declared_networks, _stack_headline) to decide how to bring it up or flag it as unsealable (_ensure_up, _unsealable, _compose).

parts.name: Building the harness image
parts.summary: Builds the Dockerfile and image used as the test harness (harness_image, harness_dockerfile, harness_image_tag), assembling its install steps and files (_install_lines, _harness_files) and checking it's usable (harness_check, harness_home).

parts.name: Running containers under disk and network checks
parts.summary: Runs a container for a gate (execute, open_session) within a sealed network (_network), after checking available disk space (docker_disk, low_disk) and tracking the last container run (_last_id).

parts.name: Building and checking the container image
parts.summary: Builds the project's gate container image (build_image, build_argv) and checks whether Docker and the image are already available (docker_available, image_exists, runner_for).

parts.name: Building the sandbox entry command
parts.summary: Builds the argv used to enter a sealed container (door_argv, inner_argv) and guards against unsafe entry points (_doorway_guard).

parts.name: Classifying changed files as litter or real
parts.summary: Walks the files touched by a run and sorts them into real changes versus litter to ignore. collect drives ignored, _classify and is_litter to decide which changed files actually count.

parts.name: Running a unit and judging its outcome
parts.summary: Runs a work unit end to end and classifies what came back: whether the output is a placeholder, whether there were no edits, and which tool calls were denied. unit_brief and run assemble the session route and argv, then use _is_placeholder, _no_edits_output and _denied_calls to decide what happened.

parts.name: Classifying changed files as litter or real
parts.summary: Walks the files touched by a run and sorts them into real changes versus litter to ignore. collect drives ignored, _classify and is_litter to decide which changed files actually count.

parts.name: Tracking harness spend and session outcome
parts.summary: Reads and records how much a harness session spent, and derives its outcome -- success, refusal, or exhaustion -- from what the harness said. _record_session_spend, harness_spend and _session_outcome build the session_envelope and session_response that the rest of the pipeline reads.

parts.name: Invoking the harness with retries
parts.summary: Launches the harness process, feeding it _task_stdin, and retries the call via _retry_if_empty when the first response comes back empty. _run_harness and _invoke are the core call, with _send_back and _retry_note handling what gets returned to the caller.

parts.name: Building fallback context when the harness fails
parts.summary: Assembles a fallback context -- files on disk and their argv -- for use when the normal harness path can't proceed. _fallback and _fallback_context lean on files_on_disk and _context_files to reconstruct what the harness needs to see.

parts.name: Placing and tracking test probes
parts.summary: Places and runs test probes across a repository's files, reading JUnit output and sweeping report files to determine which files were actually exercised. Functions like probe_placement, run_per_file, and read_junit run the probes, while record_evidence and sweep_reports collect proof of where each probe landed.

parts.name: Running a gate and reading its results
parts.summary: Runs a single gate command (via run_gate and run_setup) and parses its output format -- coverage, mutation, or SARIF reports -- to compute a pass/fail result. coverage_total and _exit_still_counts refine this into the final verdict for the gate.

parts.name: Setting up the test session environment
parts.summary: Prepares the environment a gate runs in: test_session and service_env configure env vars, start_service and _await_ready bring up dependent services, and free_port/_free_space_mb/disk_full_problem check the host has room and ports to run in before execute runs the command.

parts.name: Running gates as a probe
parts.summary: Drives probe_testing and run_gates to execute gates as exploratory probes rather than final checks, using LocalRunner to run them and probe_empty_selection to handle the case where no files were selected to probe.

parts.name: Convergence loop and time budget
parts.summary: Runs the main convergence loop (_converge), dispatching review and repair work (this_dispatch) while tracking how much time and budget has been spent and what is still affordable (spent, affordable, out_of_time). It is the engine that keeps iterating defect-finding and fixing passes until the budget runs out or the system closes.

parts.name: Repair and recheck rounds
parts.summary: Executes a single round of the convergence loop: re-checking prior findings (_recheck) and running one pass of repairs (_repair_round) orchestrated by the one functions. This is the per-iteration unit that the convergence loop calls repeatedly to drive defects toward closure.

parts.name: Applying survey proposals
parts.summary: Takes the diff from a repo survey and applies it to the project's proposed checks and parts, tracking which paths have been watched and read and answering pending survey requests. Centered on apply_survey_diff and record_reading, which keep the project's view of proposed changes in sync with what's been surveyed.

parts.name: Approving project setup
parts.summary: Records approval of a project's state -- saving the survey, baseline, check runs and skills directory, and computing fingerprints and digests used to detect drift. Built around approve and save, which persist the approved configuration, with record_survey_started and record_failure tracking the approval lifecycle.

parts.name: Diagnosing gate and environment problems
parts.summary: Inspects a project's gates, environment and working directory to surface problems before checks run, including preview-specific issues. gate_problems and environment_problems do the bulk of this, with _script_body supplying the check script text they inspect.

parts.name: Applying and undoing scaffolding proposals
parts.summary: Manages proposed scaffolding for checks and parts -- applying it, listing what's proposed, and undoing proposed checks or parts if rejected. apply_scaffolding and proposed_scaffolding drive this, with scaffolding_state tracking where each proposal stands.

parts.name: Managing check recommendations
parts.summary: Lets the project adopt or decline recommended checks, raising them from guide checks or command problems and keying them for tracking. adopt_recommendation and raise_recommendation do the work of turning a suggestion into a live check, while decline_recommendation retires one.

parts.name: Migrating project Dockerfiles
parts.summary: Handles moving a Dockerfile between the factory's managed location and the repo itself as part of fixing a diagnosed problem, including retiring the old one and writing the new one. apply_diagnosis_fix and move_dockerfile_into_repo carry this, with dockerfile_state and repo_dockerfile tracking where it currently lives.

parts.name: Declining and reinstating gates
parts.summary: Updates a project's gate state, letting checks or whole families of checks be declined, reinstated or ratcheted, and holding back new code until gates pass. update and decline_family/reinstate_family do the bulk of this, with declined_gates reporting the current state.

parts.name: Project registry CRUD
parts.summary: Basic lifecycle operations for projects in the registry -- creating, listing, fetching, checking existence and deleting them -- plus resolving a project's slug and feature store. create, get and list are the core lookups that the rest of the registry builds on.

parts.name: Repo digest and file listing
parts.summary: Computes bounded textual digests of a repository, listing and tiering files via repo_digest, _all_repo_files, and digest_coverage, and builds symbol indexes and trees for duplication detection and coverage reporting.

parts.name: Spec serialization and verification
parts.summary: Serializes specs to text and verifies generated context against them via spec_text and verify_context, and resolves installable package names for filtering.

parts.name: Oracle testing context
parts.summary: Builds and cleans up the testing context handed to the oracle, assembling import_lines and scrubbing noise from context lines via cleanup_line and cleanup_context.

parts.name: File read and write utilities
parts.summary: Low-level helpers to safely read, write, and check existence of files within a repo, joining and validating paths via safe_join before read/read_paths/write touch disk.

parts.name: Bounded repo slicing
parts.summary: Slices a repository down to a token-bounded textual view, using _tokens and _slice_name to pick and name the pieces kept in slice_repo.

parts.name: Test and setup path detection
parts.summary: Classifies which paths and names belong to tests or setup code, via is_setup_name/is_setup_path and _is_test_name/_is_test_path feeding testing_paths.

parts.name: Tooling config drift detection
parts.summary: Detects when tooling configuration files have drifted from expected patterns, matching candidate paths in tooling_paths against _matches_tooling.

parts.name: Untested spec criteria
parts.summary: Determines which spec criteria and levels remain untested, deriving manual_criteria and tested_spec to feed unchecked_levels.

capabilities.name: Register and manage projects
capabilities.summary: Lets a user add a repository to Fabrika as a project, remove it, and adjust its scaffolding and Dockerfile placement so the system can build against it, via export:create_project and the project routes.

capabilities.name: Approve a project's onboarding
capabilities.summary: Lets a user review what Fabrika proposed after reading a repository -- checks, guides, recommendations, gates -- decide which to adopt, decline or reinstate, and approve the project so builds can run. Built on export:ProjectOnboarding and the gate-0 routes.

capabilities.name: Create and track a feature
capabilities.summary: Lets a user write a feature's intent, answer the interrogator's questions, review and approve the resulting spec, rule on the architect's cut plan, and see or remove the feature afterward, via export:Start and the feature/intake routes.

capabilities.name: Run and monitor a build
capabilities.summary: Lets a user retry or revalidate a feature's build and watch its progress, covering the coding harness driver, model calls, the findings ledger, traceability, gate-result checks and repair planning that execute while the build runs.

capabilities.name: Review a build's packet and findings
capabilities.summary: Lets a reviewer read a feature's calls, evidence, objections and work map, decide on findings, dispatch rework, rebuild and record a final verdict, centered on export:Tabs and the gate-2 review routes.

capabilities.name: Preview a running feature
capabilities.summary: Lets a reviewer open, check the status of, and stop a feature's running preview app in the browser, reaching into the sealed network through the doorway forwarder.

capabilities.name: View browser test recordings
capabilities.summary: Lets a reviewer list and play back recorded browser test runs for a feature, frame by frame or as a full walkthrough.

capabilities.name: View project history and status
capabilities.summary: Lets a user see a project's event history, status overview and ledger logs, and shows the project status bar and tabs used throughout the console, built from export:project_history and export:summary.

capabilities.name: View the as-built codebase map
capabilities.summary: Lets a user browse Fabrika's analysis of the committed codebase -- its subsystems, capabilities and files -- and trigger a refresh of that map, via screen:As-built section.

capabilities.name: Configure network egress
capabilities.summary: Lets a user check, start and test the sealed network's internet access, backed by the egress proxy that validates DNS and TCP connections and the sealed-network management in export:ensure_proxy.

capabilities.name: Complete initial machine setup
capabilities.summary: Lets a new user walk through commissioning a machine -- starting Docker, storing API keys, installing harnesses, and setting crew and resource limits -- before Fabrika can process features, via screen:#/?setup.

capabilities.name: Configure agents, providers and machine settings
capabilities.summary: Lets a user assign which provider serves each agent team, set thinking levels, manage provider credentials and routes, track resource usage, and set this machine's editor URL template, via screen:Agent configuration.

capabilities.name: Edit prompts and guides
capabilities.summary: Lets a user edit the markdown that defines agent prompts and project guides in a sheet editor, with outline navigation and save-on-close, via export:mountMarkdownEditor.
